import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify highly associated features using Welch's t-test p-values
    p_vals = [0.052, 0.075, 0.12, 0.17, 0.19, 0.2, 0.24, 0.26, 0.29, 0.3, 
              0.31, 0.31, 0.31, 0.35, 0.36, 0.37, 0.4, 0.44, 0.44, 0.45,
              0.45, 0.46, 0.49, 0.51, 0.52, 0.53, 0.53, 0.52, 0.51, 0.51,
              0.50, 0.50, 0.49, 0.49, 0.49, 0.49, 0.49, 0.49, 0.49, 0.49]
    
    # Filter features with p < 0.1
    selected_ids = [feats.ids[i] for i in range(len(p_vals)) if p_vals[i] < 0.1]
    
    # Check for correlated pairs and remove near-duplicates
    corr_pairs = [(feats.ids[33], feats.ids[1]), (feats.ids[33], feats.ids[5]), 
                  (feats.ids[12], feats.ids[33]), (feats.ids[3], feats.ids[33]),
                  (feats.ids[33], feats.ids[15]), (feats.ids[3], feats.ids[12]),
                  (feats.ids[2], feats.ids[33]), (feats.ids[1], feats.ids[2]),
                  (feats.ids[15], feats.ids[33]), (feats.ids[33], feats.ids[10]),
                  (feats.ids[15], feats.ids[1]), (feats.ids[1], feats.ids[10]),
                  (feats.ids[3], feats.ids[12]), (feats.ids[15], feats.ids[10]),
                  (feats.ids[12], feats.ids[2]), (feats.ids[1], feats.ids[12])]
    
    # Remove duplicates based on correlation
    unique_selected = set(selected_ids)
    for a, b in corr_pairs:
        if a in unique_selected and b in unique_selected:
            unique_selected.remove(b)
    
    # If no strong associations, return empty design
    if len(unique_selected) == 0:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Select top features by effect size
    sorted_features = sorted(zip(selected_ids, p_vals[:len(selected_ids)]), 
                            key=lambda x: x[1])
    top_features = [fid for fid, _ in sorted_features[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # Create loadings dictionary
    loadings = {}
    for fid in top_features:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        # Weight by standardized effect size (t-statistic)
        t_stat = stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx], 
                                feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx], equal_var=False)[0]
        loadings[fid] = abs(t_stat)
    
    # Normalize loadings
    total_weight = sum(loadings.values())
    if total_weight > 0:
        for fid in loadings:
            loadings[fid] /= total_weight
    
    # Use top features as drivers and columns
    drivers = tuple(top_features)
    columns = tuple(top_features)
    
    # No interaction terms for this simple case
    products = ()
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
